entry.title: France Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform: An Overview of the Information Available
entry.content:
Hi everyone,
Many of you have already started working on the mandate for electronic invoicing and reporting reform for France, which introduces the mandatory digital invoice exchange and reporting of taxable transactions through an approved platform. 

In this blog post, I would like to share an overview of the information that's available for you when using electronic reporting via an approved platform. 

Legal Requirement and Scope 

France’s compliance reform is based on two pillars: electronic invoicing and electronic reporting. The scope of electronic invoicing covers domestic B2B transactions, payment data for services, and down payments for goods and services. Electronic reporting, by contrast, covers domestic and international B2C transactions, international B2B transactions (including exports, intra-Community supplies, and other cross-border transactions), payment data for services, and down payments for goods and services.

The determining factor is establishment in France for VAT purposes, rather than merely holding a French VAT registration number. Companies established in France may therefore be subject to both pillars. Foreign companies that are registered for VAT in France but are not established in France for VAT purposes have no electronic invoicing obligation. However, they may be subject to electronic reporting for transactions carried out in France for which they are liable for VAT.

For more information on the legal requirement and the announcement of upcoming deliveries for France Electronic Invoicing and Reporting, see SAP Regulatory Change Manager. 

 

More Information about New Features and Updates 

Implementation Overview SAP Note 

A starting point for checking the features that are made available is the Overview Implementation SAP Note. For the France mandate, there are two relevant overview SAP Notes: 

  • For electronic invoicing: SAP Note 3413565. 
  • For electronic reporting: SAP Note 3713986. 

Although our focus in this blog post is on electronic reporting, there are some technical dependencies with the electronic invoicing solution. Therefore, always check the prerequisites stated in the SAP Notes before implementing anything.

Tip: The links above take you to the latest version of the documentation of that product. Depending on the release of your system, make sure you select the specific release to display the relevant information for your system release: 

 

 

WorkZone Group 

The WorkZone group is available to help the community address questions, learn from other experiences, and used to announce daily updates in case there's a known issue, for example, if the government system is down. See France - SAP Document and Reporting Compliance. Stay tuned! 

 

Troubleshooting and FAQ 

As we learn from your experiences and business scenarios, we gather that information and include it in SAP Knowledge-Based Articles. For France Electronic Reporting, see 3756217 - eDocument France via Approved Platform Troubleshooting Guide. 

If you haven't found information on the channels above, you can use the support channel and open a customer case to the following component: CA-GTF-CSC-EDO-FR-RE. 

Please read through the information that is provided first, and you can also use the Feedback option on the Help Portal to help us understand whether the information is helpful. Please leave your comment so that we learn what didn't go well when you looked for specific information - That will guide us to the next improvements.

Stay tuned for upcoming blog posts on electronic reporting. 

Until next time,

entry.title: How to modify the Legacy Data Transfer date - SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
entry.content:
If you only create new asset master data without any postings, then you can delete the legacy asset first and then edit the Legacy Data Transfer date.

If a posting has already been made, even after it is reversed, the asset still cannot be deleted, and therefore the Legacy Data Transfer date cannot be modified.

KBA 3152945 - Cannot set an earlier LDT segment date in App Make Company Code settings -SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

If you are using the Q system, you can perform a reset through the Reset Transaction Data job: https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_CLOUD/3e5fcf2c768746049b5627bd5a42f720/a454d02b33f74db9b0f8d44c3b0061d7.html?version=LATEST&ai=true&locale=en-US

If you are using the P system, then the reset function will not be supported.

You may consider the following approach:

  1. After you reverse all the journal entries, block these assets to prevent anyone from using them later.

  2. Change the status of the segment with Legacy Data Transfer date (old date) to complete in the Make Company Code Settings app.

  3. Create a new segment, set the Legacy Data Transfer date to new date, and set the status to Ongoing / Ongoing (Other Postings Allowed).

  4. Continue to migrate the asset master data and postings that you want.

entry.title: France Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform: Key Differences Across Products and Releases
entry.content:
Hi everyone,


This blog post continues our series on France Electronic Reporting.

In case you missed the previous blog posts: 

  • See France Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform: An Overview of the Information Available for an overview of the information that is available to help you navigate on the mandate. 
  • See France Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform: Settings Checklist Based on Business Scenarios for a settings checklist based on business scenarios. 

In this blog post, I would like to share some differences across products and releases that are worth pointing out. 

 

Differences Across Products and Releases to Keep in Mind 

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, SAP S/4HANA 2021 and higher, your entry point is the Run Statutory Reports app (App ID: F1515). For more information on statutory reports, see: 

  • SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Statutory Reporting 
  • SAP S/4HANA: Statutory Reporting  

Within the app, you select the report you want to run, and you can use the Manage Electronic Documents reporting activity that takes you to the Manage Electronic Documents app (App ID: F4306). You can use the Source for Invoice Reporting and Source for Payment Reporting processes to check the eDocuments that are created for a reporting period. You can also perform actions, such as change the tax reporting date of electronic documents before they are included in a list. 

Once you're ready, you can prepare the report run. Differently from lower releases, you check the statuses of the report submission within the Run Statutory Reports app, and once a report run is available, you can also show statutory reports from the Manage Electronic Documents app.  Note that the document status and report run status might not get updated immediately. Once a response is received from the authorities, you can view the response file in the document status log.

After a list has been submitted and accepted by authority, you can generate a rectification by starting a new phase if you want to add or remove an eDocument from a reporting period by changing the tax reporting date. Currently, to remove an eDocument from a list, you can post a credit memo with a reference to the initial invoice.  

Tip:  

  • You can use the Run Statutory Reports - France e-Reporting  app (ID: F1515_FR_4) to run the reports specific for France Electronic Reporting. For more information, see SAP Note  3721231 .
  • If you're new to using the Manage Electronic Documents app, you can find more information on the differences between the Fiori app and the Cockpit (available in lower releases) here: What are the differences between the Manage Electronic Documents app and eDocument Cockpit app? | SAP Help Portal. 

Remember: In Fiori apps, you can find more information about specific fields and process statuses when you select the Question Marc icon on the top right of the screen. A side panel displays more information about specific fields. 

For more information on the procedure to generate each report, see: 

  • SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Generating the Customer Invoice List, Generating the Supplier Invoice List, Generating the Payment List. 
  • SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2021 and higher: Generating the Customer Invoice List, Generating the Supplier Invoice List, and Generating the Payment List. 

 

In SAP S/4HANA 2020 and below, and in SAP ERP, you can use the eDocument Cockpit (transaction EDOC_COCKPIT) and the Source for Invoice Reporting (FRIVREPSRC) and Source for Payment Reporting (FRPYREPSRC) processes to display the eDocuments that are created for a reporting period. You can also perform actions, such as change the tax reporting date or cancel electronic documents before they are included in a list. 

Once you have the relevant eDocuments created for a reporting period, you run the Create Lists of Electronic Documents report (transaction EDOC_FR_EREP) to generate the lists. You then go back to the eDocument Cockpit (transaction EDOC_COCKPIT) and you use the processes Invoice Reporting (FRINVREP_E) and Payment Reporting (FRPAYREP_E) to display the lists that have been generated, submit them to the authorities, and check the report submission statuses. 

  • SAP S/4HANA 2020 and below: Generating Customer Invoice Reporting, Generating Supplier Invoice Reporting, and Generating Payment Reporting.  
  • SAP ERP: Generating Customer Invoice Reporting, Generating Supplier Invoice Reporting, and Generating Payment Reporting. 

After a list has been submitted and accepted by authority, you can generate a rectification if you want to add or remove an eDocument from a reporting period by changing the tax reporting date. Currently, to remove an eDocument from a list, you can post a credit memo with a reference to the initial invoice. For more information on the rectification, see: 

  • SAP S/4HANA 2020 and below: Correcting Data After Submitting the Customer Invoice Reporting to the Tax Authority, Correcting Data After Submitting the Supplier Invoice Reporting to the Tax Authority, and Correcting Data After Submitting the Payment Reporting to the Tax Authority.    
  • SAP ERP: Correcting Data After Submitting the Customer Invoice Reporting to the Tax Authority, Correcting Data After Submitting the Supplier Invoice Reporting to the Tax Authority, and Correcting Data After Submitting the Payment Reporting to the Tax Authority.     

 

We hope that this overview helps you find the information you need for the product you use and for your system release. Let us know if you have questions in the comments section below. 

Best regards, 

Ailane Kuhn

entry.title: AI-Assisted Role Wizard: Let your work speak for itself
entry.content:
Since introducing the Role-based Process Overview capability, people across organizations have been able to immediately see which processes are relevant to their work. Now, we're taking it one step further because finding the right role shouldn't require knowing your dictionary inside and out. 

We're excited to announce an AI-driven enhancement to the Role-based Process Overview capability: an access aware intelligent setup wizard that finds relevant roles for you, based on how you describe your own work. 

To enable AI-assisted Role-based Process Overview capability, your administrator needs to accept AI Terms and Conditions. 

No dictionary expertise required 

The original setup wizard asks you to select roles from your organization's dictionary. That works well when you already know what's in there but for new joiners, cross-functional contributors, or anyone switching teams, browsing an unfamiliar dictionary to find your roles can slow things down before you've even started. 

With the AI-powered role wizard, you simply describe what you do and the wizard handles the matching. 

How it works 

Getting started is even easier now: 

  1. Find "My Process Overview" — Log in and locate the My Process Overview panel on the home page, just as before. 
  2. Start the Quick Setup — On your first visit, you'll see Role Wizard and can initiate it directly. Already have your profile set up? You can re-run it anytime to refine your roles or start fresh. 
  3. Describe your role and responsibilities — Instead of browsing the dictionary, type a short description of your job: your team, your tasks, what you own. The AI-driven wizard reads your input and surfaces the dictionary roles most relevant to you. 
  4. Review and confirm — The wizard presents its suggestions. You stay in control: accept, adjust, or add roles before confirming. 
  5. Enjoy your personalized view — Your My Process Overview generates automatically, showing the processes, activities, and RACI assignments tied to your confirmed roles. 

Why it matters 

The biggest friction point in the original setup was the expectation that users already know their organization's role taxonomy. That's a reasonable ask for a process owner but not for someone on day one, or someone who spans multiple functions. 

By letting users describe their work in plain language and having AI close the gap to the dictionary, setup becomes accessible to everyone, regardless of how familiar they are with your organization's dictionary. 

This means: 

  • Faster time-to-value: New joiners can set up a meaningful process view in minutes, without a guided tour of the dictionary first 
  • Better role matching: Describing responsibilities often surfaces relevant roles users wouldn't have found by browsing alone 
  • The same personalized outcome: Everything that made Role-based Process Overview capability powerful such as access-aware content, RACI visibility, single-page clarity, remains exactly in place but now further accelerated by AI 

Check out the demo video to learn about the details

entry.title: The depreciation results differ between the two currencies - SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
entry.content:
After running depreciation, upon comparing the Company Code currency and Global Currency, the exchange rate did not use the one defined by the customer.

The depreciation run does NOT translate the posting amounts for the individual currencies. In fact the currency translation takes place for the asset acquisition posting with the given posting parameters (posting date, etc.).

For example, an asset has the initial acquisition posting in period 11. The acquisition posting was done with 26,500.00 MYR

(= Company Code Currency). This posting amount was translated to 5,640.70 USD (= Group Currency).

Once the acquisition is posted, the system then calculates the depreciation amounts for each currency type (Currency Type = Company Code Currency or Group Currency).

The depreciation parameters for this asset in depreciation area 01 are currently:

  • Depreciation Key: LINK (= APC over Useful Life)
  • Useful Life: 10 Years and 0 Periods

Hence the system calculates the following depreciation amounts:

  1. Company Code Currency (MYR)

Depreciation 2023 = 26,500 MYR x 10% [= 1/10] x 2 / 12 [2 periods pro rata for periods 11 & 12]
= 441.67 MYR

As the rounding setting is set to round the net book value, this calculated amount is adjusted to 442.00 MYR.

  1. Group Currency (USD)

Depreciation 2023 = 5,640.70 USD x 10% [= 1/10] x 2 / 12 [2 periods pro rata for periods 11 & 12]
= 94.01 USD

As the rounding setting is set to round the net book value, this calculated amount is adjusted to 94.00 USD.

As shown above, the currency translation does not take place at the time of the depreciation posting. This is necessary so that the (original) APC is distributed evenly over the useful life. If the currency translation were to take place at every depreciation posting, it could not be ensured that the net book value reaches zero at the end of the useful life.

The amounts in different currencies can be viewed in the app "Manage Fixed Asset". In the valuation section for depreciation area 01, there is a dropdown list in the upper right corner of the value display control, in which the individual currency types can be selected.

entry.title: BTPEA Is Now Available in China: Bringing Consumption-Based Flexibility to SAP BAIP Customers
entry.content:
SAP BTP Enterprise Agreement (BTPEA) was officially released in China on May 21, 2026 (SKU 8016044), bringing a consumption-based commercial model to SAP BAIP customers in the China market.

Why Is BTPEA in China an Important Milestone?

The launch of BTPEA in China marks an important step in expanding the commercial options available to SAP BAIP customers, creating opportunities to onboard more services into the local portfolio, and providing greater flexibility in how customers consume SAP BAIP services.

1. Introducing a Consumption-Based Commercial Model to China

Before BTPEA became available in China, Subscription was the only commercial model available to SAP BAIP customers in the China market. The introduction of BTPEA expands the available commercial choices beyond subscription-based commitments.

While Subscription is well suited to predictable workloads and predefined service requirements, BTPEA provides greater flexibility for customers whose consumption needs may change over time. Customers can use prepaid cloud credits across eligible services, switch between services as business requirements evolve, and pay for actual consumption within the terms of their BTPEA contract.

This flexibility is particularly valuable for customers exploring new use cases, managing fluctuating workloads, adopting services for which long-term consumption requirements are difficult to predict, or combining predictable subscription commitments with consumption-based cloud credits for more experimental workloads.

2. Enabling a Broader SAP BAIP Service Portfolio in China

Some SAP BAIP services are offered exclusively through the consumption-based commercial model. With BTPEA now available in China, more services can be considered for onboarding into the China market. For example, the following services are consumption-based only and are now available in China through BTPEA: Kyma runtime, SAP Build Work Zone advanced edition, Task Center, SAP Forms Service by Adobe, Object Store, Transport Management, Data Privacy Integration, etc.

This creates opportunities to expand the SAP BAIP service portfolio available to customers in China and helps make the China offering more complete and aligned with the evolving global portfolio.

Ultimately, a broader service portfolio gives customers more opportunities to access SAP BAIP capabilities and select the services that best meet their business needs.

What Is SAP BTPEA?

SAP BTP Enterprise Agreement (BTPEA) is a consumption-based commercial model that allows customers to consume eligible SAP BAIP services using prepaid cloud credits.

Under this model, customers make an upfront investment in cloud credits for the contract duration, with an annual commitment to consume SAP BAIP services. The cost of actual consumption is deducted from the available cloud credit balance.

BTPEA is particularly suitable for customers with established business plans who need flexibility to activate and deactivate services, switch between eligible services, and accommodate changing resource requirements without committing to a single service throughout the contract duration.

Key benefits include:

  • Flexibility: Switch between eligible SAP BAIP services as business requirements evolve.
  • Consumption transparency: Receive a monthly balance statement detailing service consumption and the corresponding costs.
  • Simplified commercial management: Use prepaid cloud credits across eligible services instead of managing separate subscription commitments for every service.
  • Volume-based discounts: Benefit from volume-based discounts, subject to the applicable commercial terms.
  • Access to an evolving service catalog: Access new SAP BAIP services as they become available under the consumption-based commercial model.

Customers are billed annually in advance. Any consumption exceeding the available cloud credit balance is billed in arrears at list price. Customers can purchase additional cloud credits at any time to help prevent overages.

BTPEA in China: Service Availability

Service availability varies by country, region, and contract terms. Customers can use the following resources to check which services are available in China and review the applicable pricing information.

1. SAP Discovery Center — Service Availability and Pricing Overview

Visit SAP Discovery Center

The SAP Discovery Center provides a non-legally binding reference for service availability and pricing. Customers can filter by Regions and Commercial Model to identify services available in China under BTPEA.

China currently has two available regions:

  • China (North 3) — cn20
  • China (Shanghai) — cn40

Note that not all services are available in both regions.

2. SAP BTPEA Price List — Contractual Reference

Visit the SAP BTPEA Price List

The SAP BTPEA Price List provides legally binding contract documentation. Customers can filter by Country and Contract Start Date to check service availability and pricing applicable to their contracts.

Please refer to the applicable contractual documentation for the final commercial terms.

Combining Subscription and Consumption-Based Models with a Hybrid Account

Many customers have existing SAP BAIP subscription contracts while also needing the flexibility of consumption-based services. A hybrid account supports both commercial models within the same SAP BAIP global account, allowing customers to combine predictable subscription commitments with consumption-based cloud credits.

This approach offers several benefits:

  • Reduced administration effort: Both subscription and BTPEA contracts can coexist under the same SAP BTP global account, so development and service consumption are managed in a single environment.
  • Commit more, save more — and pay only for what you use: Lock in attractive volume discounts through subscription commitments for predictable workloads, while using BTPEA cloud credits to cover peak periods or exploration projects where resource requirements are uncertain.

How Does Charging Work in a Hybrid Account?

The charging mechanism follows the applicable subscription entitlement quota and the consumption-based model.

When customers consume services covered by their subscription entitlement quota, that consumption is covered by the subscription model. Once consumption exceeds the subscription entitlement quota, the excess consumption is charged under the consumption-based model, using the available cloud credits.

This arrangement allows customers to retain their existing subscription commitments while using BTPEA to accommodate additional consumption.

China-Specific Considerations

While BTPEA is now available in China, there are a few operational considerations customers should be aware of.

1. Cockpit Cost and Usage Visibility

The Cost and Usage tabs in SAP BAIP Cockpit are available for the consumption-based offering in China, providing customers with visibility into their consumption and related costs.

Most of the planned Cockpit functionality is available. However, the Budget module is not yet fully available in the China offering.

Customers should take this limitation into account when planning their cost-monitoring processes. Further updates will be communicated as the remaining functionality becomes available.

2. Balance Statement Email Distribution

In the global process, balance statement (BS) emails are sent directly to customers. China follows a different process due to the role of CDC.

In China, CDC acts as SAP's third-party contracting partner — customers sign contracts with CDC rather than directly with SAP. As a result, all balance statement emails would be routed to CDC first, for centralized translation and forwarding to customers.

Key Resources You Should Know

The following resources are essential reading for getting started with BTPEA — covering the consumption-based commercial model, consumption monitoring, and balance statement verification.

  • SAP Help Portal: What Is the Consumption-Based Commercial Model? — Learn about the principles and benefits of the consumption-based commercial model.
  • SAP Help Portal: Monitoring Usage and Consumption Costs in Your Global Account — Understand how to monitor service usage and consumption costs.
  • SAP Learning: Verifying the Balance Statement — Learn how to review and verify balance statements.
  • SAP Document: FAQ Consumption-Based Commercial Model CPEA & Cloud Credits — Find answers to frequently asked questions about consumption-based commercial models and cloud credits.
